title: Owls Can't Move Their Eyes
fact: Owls cannot move their eyes because their eyes are tube-shaped and fixed in the skull, so they turn their heads up to about 270 degrees instead.
narration: Owls can't move their eyes. Their eyes aren't balls like ours. They're long tubes, locked in place inside the skull. So to look sideways, an owl has to turn its whole head, and it can twist it most of the way round, about three quarters of a full circle. That stare isn't attitude. It simply can't look away.
caption:
That owl isn't judging you. It just can't look anywhere else.

An owl's eyes aren't round like ours. They're shaped more like tubes and they're fixed in place, so the bird can't glance left or right at all. To make up for it, an owl can swing its head about three quarters of the way around. I tried to imagine living like that and gave up after ten seconds.

Could you cope if you had to turn your whole head every time you wanted to look at something?

title: One Pineapple Takes Two Years
hook: One pineapple takes two years to grow
fact: A pineapple plant takes about 18 to 24 months to produce a single fruit, and each plant makes only one pineapple at a time.
narration: One pineapple takes two years to grow. And each plant makes just one at a time, sitting on top like a crown. It starts as a cluster of purple flowers that slowly fuse into a single fruit. Farmers wait about twenty months for it. So that slice on your plate took longer to make than a human baby.
caption:
I'll never rush a pineapple again.

One plant grows exactly one pineapple at a time, and it takes close to two years to get there. It starts out as a bunch of little purple flowers that join together into a single fruit. That means the pineapple in your kitchen was in the ground for longer than it takes to make a baby. Kind of puts the price in perspective.

Did you think they grew on trees too, or was that just me?

title: Which One Is True: Goldfish, Flamingos, Bats
hook: Two of these are myths. Which one is true?
fact: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance; goldfish can remember things for months, not three seconds; and bats are not blind.
narration: Two of these are myths. Which one is true? A. Goldfish only remember things for three seconds. B. A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance. C. Bats are completely blind. Got your answer? It's B. Flamboyance is the real word for a flock of flamingos. Goldfish remember for months, and bats can see just fine.
caption:
Two of these are things everyone repeats, and they're wrong.

Goldfish don't forget everything in three seconds. They can remember things for months, and people have trained them to do simple tricks. Bats aren't blind either. They can all see, and many see pretty well. The only true one is the flamingo one, and honestly it's the one that sounds made up.

Which one did you pick before the answer came up?

title: Three Things About Honeybees
hook: Can you tell what this is?
fact: Honeybees have five eyes, a single worker bee makes about one twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its lifetime, and bees can learn to recognise human faces.
narration: Can you tell what this is? It's a honeybee, and here are three things you didn't know about it. One. It has five eyes: two big ones, and three tiny ones on top of its head. Two. In its whole life, one bee makes about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey. Three. Bees can learn to recognise human faces. Which one surprised you most?
caption:
I looked at a jar of honey differently after this.

A honeybee has five eyes, two big ones on the sides and three tiny ones on top of its head. One bee makes about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its whole life, so a single spoonful is the life's work of a dozen bees. And in experiments, bees have learned to tell human faces apart. Not bad for something that small.

Which of the three surprised you most?
